nodes.title: Intake module: chunked or one-shot 20 MB uploads, mapping with per-row preview, one write path by authority and freshness, signed idempotent contacts webhook, append-only consent, suppression, DPDP erase with tombstones, DND seam, audiences
nodes.details: 21 tools, 2 raw routes, migration 0101. 18/18 tests (node:test, throwaway Postgres 16). Not verified: XLSX/Sheets, unmerge, conflict resolution, real NCPR lookup, concurrent overlapping commits, a full 20 MB commit, erasure of transcripts and recordings.

nodes.title: A 50,000-row CSV (2.94 MB, 7 columns, 50 Excel-mangled rows) imports in one transaction in 19.4-21.7 s; re-importing it (all rows update) takes 11.7-14.5 s
nodes.method: product/tests/intake-scale.test.ts: upload in 4 parts over HTTP, source.map, then source.commit via registry.execute; throwaway Postgres 16 on the coding sandbox (4 vCPU, 15 GB); 5 runs alone, 3 inside the full suite at concurrency 4; wall-clock around the commit call

nodes.title: A tenant's own file uploads count as one lineage: a newer upload replaces an older upload's value at equal authority; only different systems at equal rank go to review
nodes.rationale: The blueprint's rule (equal authorities with different values go to review) applied literally to uploads sent every row of a monthly re-upload to review. Uploads are one asserter, the tenant.
nodes.reverse_if: Tenants keep several independent lists (different branches or vendors) whose values for the same person legitimately disagree, and review is wanted between them; then make lineage per source and ask at commit.

nodes.title: Sending equal-authority disagreements between two uploads to review
nodes.tried: decide(): equal authority from a different source_id means conflict_review, applied to every source including file uploads.
nodes.broke: The 50k re-import test: 49,950 rows went to review and 0 updated, because each upload is its own source.

nodes.title: DPDP erase_me keeps the contact row as a husk (e164 'erased:<id>', no name or attributes) instead of deleting it
nodes.rationale: consent_record and suppression cascade on contact delete (0002). Deleting the person would delete the consent history and the suppression the erasure must keep. The tombstone (HMAC of the number, per-workspace salt) blocks re-creation; suppressions are re-keyed to the hash.
nodes.reverse_if: The consent and suppression ledgers stop referencing contact with ON DELETE CASCADE (e.g. they key on e164_hash), so the row can be deleted outright.

nodes.title: A value past its max age loses its authority: a newer observation from a lower authority replaces it
nodes.rationale: Freshness bounds authority (blueprint §2, DataAuthorityClaim max_age). A month-old CRM amount should not beat today's upload of the same field.
nodes.reverse_if: A record subject from the system of record (rank 100) is overwritten by a stale-but-correct case in practice; then exempt rank 100 or mark the replacement for review.

nodes.title: DND unknown, never checked, or checked more than 7 days ago is 'unknown', and contact.dial_facts blocks promotional calls on it; service calls are not blocked by DND
nodes.rationale: Task brief: unknown DND is a fact the dial gate treats as fail-closed for promotional. On 140xx the operator scrubs too (trust-telephony M4). The real NCPR adapter stays disabled until a licensed lookup is contracted.
nodes.reverse_if: Counsel or the carrier contract says service calls must also respect NCPR, or a fresher bound than 7 days is required.

nodes.title: The intake 50k scale test failed once, on the first full-suite run (concurrency 4, fresh database), and the reason was not captured; three later full runs and five solo runs passed
nodes.closes_when: Ten full-suite runs with captured output show no failure, or the failure recurs and its error is recorded.

nodes.title: Webhook HMAC secrets sit in plaintext in intake_source.hook_secret until a vault exists
nodes.closes_when: Secrets move to the workspace vault with a rotate tool, and the column is dropped.

events.details: Intake module pushed: 21 tools, uploads and a signed contacts webhook, migration 0101; 18/18 intake tests and 173/173 product tests (3 of 4 full runs) on the throwaway Postgres. Verified: phone edge cases, authority and dedupe, append-only consent, suppression on re-import, DPDP tombstone and suppression, webhook signature and idempotency, tenancy, DND fail-closed, 50k rows in 19.4-21.7 s (n=8). Not verified: XLSX, real NCPR, concurrent overlapping commits, a 20 MB commit, transcript erasure.
